newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar ends stronger on steady U.S. rates.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar ends stronger on steady U.S. rates.

text.p: * Canada's dollar ended stronger at C$1.3668 (US$0.7316) from this morning's open of C$1.3725 (US$0.7285) after it was reported that the Federal Reserve held U.S. rates steady.
* Traders said the Canadian dollar rallied on the news which is seen as allowing the Bank of Canada to keep short-term Canaian interest rates low.
"This is good news for Canada, and that is being reflected in the price of the Canadian dollar," Farrill said.

The Canadian dollar has been under pressure from international investors since the Federal Reserve raised interest rates on March 25 and the Bank of Canada held its own rates steady. Economists have said that if the Bank of Canada resisted another raise from the Fed the spread on interest rates between Canada and the U.S. would widen. Such a widening would encourage a selloff in the Canadian dollar by attracting investors to sell Canadian short-term debt instruments in favor of similar U.S. treasuries with much higher yields.
On Thursday, the Canadian dollar staged its biggest one-day rally since the 1994 Quebec provincial election, gaining more than one U.S. cent against the U.S. dollar.
The rally was sparked by Bank of Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen who said there was a need for a less stimulative monetary policy.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar fell to 82.41 yen from Friday's close of 84.28 and eased to 1.2275 marks from Friday's 1.2456 marks.
Canadian financial markets were closed on Monday due to a holiday.
